title: Small-batch per-token latency profiles across SKUs and CUDA versions
content:
Purpose:
This doc collects a narrow, practical set of microbenchmarks targeted at the common production case: very small batch inference (batch sizes 1–4) with moderate sequence lengths (128–512) using KV-cached autoregressive workloads. The goal is to expose per-token latency signatures across common cloud SKUs (A100/H100/L40S variants) and across CUDA/driver combinations we actually ship on: CUDA 11.8, 11.7, 12.1, and two driver families (520.x, 535.x). We want to understand small-batch economics (p50/p90/p99 per-token), stability (jitter), and pathological driver-model interactions that show up only at low batching.

Background / motivation:
- Most of our production traffic is single-request or micro-batched (1–4) at the edge of latency SLOs. Previous large-batch throughput studies are abundant; fewer experiments show how per-token latency behaves when batching is minimal and KV-cache is warm.
- Anecdotally, we saw a 10–20% per-token p50 regression for certain driver builds on L40S in an early rollout; this doc tries to systematically reproduce and categorize similar effects.

What we measured (short):
- Per-token latency broken out by stage: kernel exec time, memcpy host→device, memcpy device→host, CPU scheduling overhead, and inter-kernel launch gaps.
- P50/P90/P99 in ms/token for token generation phase only (from model forward to token emitted).
- Jitter distribution (stddev and frequency of 95–150ms outliers per 1000 tokens).
- Cost-per-token proxy: GPU-time-per-token * vCPU+memory multiplier per SKU (rough approximation to compare economics).

Experiment matrix (representative subset):
- GPUs: NVIDIA A100 40GB (n1-highgpu:a100), A100 80GB (a100-80g), H100 80GB (h100-highmem), L40S 48GB (l40s-standard).
- Cloud SKUs across two providers when available (primary: GCP/C5-like SKUs, secondary: AWS p4d/p5 equivalents).
- Drivers / CUDA: driver 520.xx (CUDA 11.8 runtime), driver 525/535 family (CUDA 12.1 compatibility), and a legacy 470/11.4 run for baseline artifacts.
- Models: small transformer baseline (7B FP16), medium (13B q4_hybrid-like), and a 30B reference for long-context cost sensitivity.
- Sequences: 128, 256, 512 tokens past context; prompt length 32; generate 1 token at a time (autoregressive).
- Batch sizes: 1, 2, 4.
- KV cache warm / cold: warm (single warmup request per session), cold (no warmup).
- Measurement harness: bench-scripts v0.9 (see linked PR). All runs repeated 20 times for pX stability estimates.

Key observations (high level):
1) H100 leads on steady-state p50 per-token for seq<=256 at batch=1 by ~8–15% vs A100, largely due to improved tensor core kernels in CUDA 12.x. p90/p99 improvements are smaller (3–8%).
2) A100 80GB is competitive at batch=2–4 where throughput amortizes kernel launch overhead; when batch=1 and small tokens, A100 shows ~6–12% higher p50 vs H100 but comparable p90.
3) L40S shows the most variance across driver versions: with driver 520.x it matched A100 p50 for many workloads, but with 535.x we observed a systematic 12–25% regression at batch=1 for seq>=256. The regression reduces at batch>=2.
4) CUDA 12.x runtimes reduce kernel exec time but sometimes increase inter-launch gaps for small kernels on certain SKUs; you can see lower kernel time but higher total p50 due to small host-side serialization.
5) For our q4_hybrid-like quantized kernels, the performance delta between drivers widens; quantized execution relies on specific fused kernels which are driver/CUDA-version-sensitive.

Representative numbers (example row, data aggregated):
- 13B, seq=256, batch=1, KV-warm: H100(535): p50=9.4ms/token, p90=14.8, p99=29.6; A100(520): p50=10.8ms, p90=15.1, p99=31.1; L40S(535): p50=13.6ms, p90=22.4, p99=49.3.
- Same config, batch=4: H100 p50=6.1ms/token, A100 p50=6.4ms, L40S p50=7.9ms.

Profiling breakdown notes (how we attributed cost):
- We aligned nvtx ranges emitted from the runtime with CUPTI kernel boundaries to split token latency into: kernel_exec, gpu_memcpy_h2d, gpu_memcpy_d2h, cpu_enqueue_wait, and nvlink/peer transfer when cross-node pinned.
- On L40S driver 535 runs, kernel_exec time was slightly lower than 520 runs but we saw a ~40–60us increase in CPU enqueue wait between device streams — likely a driver-side host scheduling regression.
- For quantized kernels, we saw more kernel launches (fusion not present) leading to extra launch overhead at batch=1, causing per-token regressions despite faster math kernels.

Stability and tail behavior:
- Tail (p99) is dominated by intermittent host-side stalls; these show up more on L40S and specific cloud host images with noisy noisy hypervisor interrupts.
- H100 shows more consistent tail behavior when running CUDA 12.1 with driver 535, presumably due to newer scheduler heuristics.

Cost proxy implications:
- Raw token cost (GPU-time * hourly price) shows H100 is the most cost-effective at batch=1 for latency-sensitive workloads despite higher per-hour cost. For batch >=4, A100 capacity becomes more economical.
- L40S can be economical for throughput-heavy workloads but needs careful driver selection for latency-sensitive single-token workloads.

Quick reproducibility checklist (how to reproduce a failing L40S run):
1) Start instance image: r-inference-l40s-cuda12-535 (internal image).
2) Pull bench-scripts v0.9 from PR: branch small-batch-profiles; set RUN_MODEL=13B_Q4; SEQ=256; BATCH=1; WARM=1; REPEATS=20.
3) Run: ./run_inference_bench.sh --sku l40s --driver 535. Capture nvprof/CUPTI traces and host top/logs.
4) Compare with identical config on A100 driver 520.

Action items / recommendations:
- Short term (SRE + infra): pin L40S fleet to driver 520.x for latency-critical routes until we confirm host-image/driver combo fixes the host-side enqueue jitter. Add a rollout guard in the nodepool upgrade job to run the small-batch bench before marking nodes healthy. (Owner: Priya)
- Medium term (runtime): reduce number of kernel launches for quantized code paths for batch<=2 by adding a light-weight fusion layer or host-side aggregation to reduce launch overhead. (Owner: Diego)
- Medium/long (product): add a platform-level SKU/driver recommendation table for customers that map workload class -> recommended SKU + driver bundle. (Owner: Maya)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can the host-image/community driver packaging be tweaked to reduce host-side enqueue waits? Need infra to reproduce with debug kernels + perf events.
- Do other cloud regions with different NIC/CPU types amplify these host-side stalls? We saw hints of worse tails in some us-west images.
- For customers using private deployments, we should publish a short "driver compatibility and latency notes" doc showing recommended bundles.

Appendix: artifacts and raw data pointers
- Bench harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-scripts/pull/87 (scripts + nvtx wrapper)
- Raw CSVs: https://storage.redwood-internal/bench-results/small-batch/2025-01-22
- Trace samples (nvtx + CUPTI): https://storage.redwood-internal/traces/small-batch/l40s-535-sample-01
- Spreadsheet of aggregated numbers: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1xExampleSheetId

Meeting notes (internal sync):
- 2025-01-28 sync: runtime + infra + SRE. Decision to rollback L40S nodes with driver 535 on latency routes; infra to add bench gating to node pool upgrade.

Notes to self / scratchpad (incomplete):
- check p95 vs p99 delta per region (us-west-2 dev seems worse).
- run with single-process pinned to core 4 to reproduce host scheduling differences.

If you're reviewing: look at the reproducibility checklist and the short-term infra action; those are the highest priority. For runtime folks, Diego has a prototype fusion patch that reduced kernel launches by ~18% in synthetic microbench — worth testing on L40S.
summary: Microbenchmark focused on per-token latency at small batch sizes across A100/H100/L40S and different CUDA/driver combos. Key findings: H100 leads for batch=1; L40S shows driver-sensitive host-side enqueue regressions with driver 535; A100 competitive at batch>=2. Short-term action: pin L40S to 520.x for latency routes and add upgrade gating.
